_comment: Shipped retail vocabularies (D9). Delivered with every deployment; customers extend
them with an overlay rather than forking them (G10).
Terms here must be true of retail in general, not of one customer. A term that only
makes sense for a single deployment belongs in that deployment's overlay. The test to
apply before adding one: would the next retail customer recognise it without being
told what business we built it for?

grain.description: One row for the whole deployment. No breakdown.
One row per individual customer or contact.
One row per defined segment of customers.
One row per individual product or SKU.
One row per category in the product hierarchy.
One row per supplier or vendor.
One row per store, warehouse, region or other physical place.
One row per sales or marketing channel.
One row per order or transaction.
One row per period, at whatever calendar grain the KPI declares.

business_area.description: Who the customers are and how they behave.
What is sold, and how each product performs.
What is on hand, what is short, what is overstocked.
Running the stores and the workforce: staffing, tasks, shrink and execution.

result_shape.description: One value per grain per run. Can be thresholded and trended.
A listing. Useful to a person; cannot be alerted on or trended.

use_case_shape.description: Answers a question. Writes nothing anywhere.
Watches a condition and notifies a person when it holds. Writes nothing to a business system.
Proposes a change to a business system and waits for a person to accept it.
Makes a change to a business system without waiting for a person.

autonomy.description: Surfaces decision cards for a person to accept or reject.

feasibility.description: Every source table the formula needs is present in the semantic snapshot.
Some source tables are present and some are missing.
No source table the formula needs is present.

compliance_tag.description: Directly identifies a person: name, email, phone, address.
Identifies a person only when joined to something else -- a hashed email, a cookie or device id.
Prices, amounts, margins or terms that are commercially confidential.
Restricted by an agreement with a supplier, partner or customer rather than by law.
Nothing restricts sharing this. Stated rather than left blank, so an unreviewed field is distinguishable from a reviewed one.

_comment: What a business_area term does not carry: the label a screen shows and the subject
areas beneath the area (the retail hierarchy the API contract's BusinessArea renders).
Keyed by term value. A missing label is derived from the id. An overlay may add subject
areas to a core area and label an area it adds; it may not relabel a core area (G10).
